tasks.english: [IT39] Selfotel: the head-injury trial was stopped after a signal in a stroke study, and a later analysis did not confirm excess mortality in head injury (abstract level). Perzinfotel is NR2A-preferring. The carbenoxolone half of the gap-junction logic carries its own caveat (it is not specific to gap junctions).

[IT39] A ketogenic-diet response is reported in 3 of 5 WOREE individuals (lactate 2.4 to 3.3 mmol/L in one individual); the Pdk1 transcript and serum-lactate datum in the Wwox-null MEF and mouse paper is non-neural and measures no PDH.

[IT39 dream] In the same lines, read the HIF and glycolytic target genes beside the neuronal genes, and add a HIF1A or EPAS1 knockdown arm for the glycolytic readout: a MYC to HIF1A edge exists at database level (sign context-dependent) and HIF-axis data exist in WWOX cells (non-neural), so the MYC change could act on glycolysis, be reached from it, or follow a shared maturation or composition change; the measurement separates these (exploratory, no compound).

[IT39] Model identity of the conditional line is Synapsin-Cre; a statement of zero hits for parvalbumin loss is wrong (about 44 percent fewer PV-positive cells in the 2-week full-knockout hippocampus); perineuronal-net counter-evidence exists and two explanations of an external report are mutually inconsistent.

[IT39] The Src and Fyn chain to NRF2 from an external report rests on a retracted article (21690096); no consumer carries the chain now, its other support is a 2007 paper from the same laboratory line (not independent), and reductive stress is a transfer from cardiac models.

[IT39] Transfer context only: two further ISR reports (VWM line, myelin readouts read in one) do not test WWOX; the biochemical report used as the bridge runs against its use; for human neural cells the absence is 'none found in two PubMed strings', the fly datum is conditional on neuronal Abeta42, and a non-neural WWOX paper links PERK and IRE1.
[IT39] The transfer from KCNQ2 and TSC is analogy; genotype stratification is established for mortality only; lithium is not the only existing-drug node (ethosuximide was also tested).

[IT39] The panel of 'structurally unrelated' antagonists is not independent: two of the listed antagonists are the same molecule under different names (one of them is Z944), and Z944 and TTA-P2 share a core chemical scaffold.

[IT39] An inositol-depletion arm is not GSK-3-free (GSK-3 alpha inactivated, beta not significantly altered; one paper, one isoform); the S9A cross is not an attribution control; time-gated dosing has no timing source.

[IT39] GSK3 context rows: a GSK3 inhibitor run after Foxg1 knockdown goes the opposite way to the inhibitor-raises-differentiation reports, and a 2026 review holds both directions; the slice paper's finding is neuron-specific wording, not oligodendrocyte-wide.

[IT39] Corrections carried from the repeat: the ketogenic paper, the MC1568 and Bdnf statement, the pooled SPR range, lithium specificity and the source type of ICP0 were each misstated in an external report; human primary muscle cells with HDAC5 knockdown show lower GLUT1 expression (opposite in sign to that report's table); a route through HDAC4, MEF2A and GLUT1 exists.

[IT39] Ivabradine blocks sag and hyperpolarises cortical L5 and L6 neurons in normal rat slices, and injection into somatosensory cortex cut absence-seizure time by 96 percent against 40 percent in thalamic VB (abstract); the GAERS authors read Ih as not an adaptive response to spike-wave discharges (input resistance fell, resting potential and sag unchanged), which sits beside the discordant precedents.
